# Canonical cli.style principles in order (1..56): `anchor title`, one per line.
# Source: spf13/cli-website content/*/*.md frontmatter (weight, anchor, title) @ 15607c6.
speak-in-sentences Speak in sentences.
structure-over-state Use subcommands, not mode flags.
unrepresentable Make invalid combinations impossible.
name-for-typing Name the application for typing.
verbs-are-verbs Few verbs, many nouns.
positional-arguments The target is positional; everything else is a flag.
end-of-flags Honor --, the end of flags.
convention-over-configuration Convention over configuration.
one-flag-one-meaning One flag, one meaning, everywhere.
long-flags-first Long flags are for scripts; short flags are for hands.
precedence-is-a-contract Precedence is a contract.
configuration-by-lifespan Match configuration to lifespan.
config-file-location Put configuration where the platform says.
run-without-config Run with no configuration at all.
be-a-filter Read stdin, write stdout; compose.
name-the-outcome Name the outcome, not the mechanism.
one-word-names Use one word whenever possible.
preview-is-a-diff Show the change, not the summary.
idempotent-or-refuse Be idempotent, or refuse.
destruction-is-deliberate Match confirmation to consequences.
least-surprise Do only what the name promises.
recognition-over-recall Recognition over recall.
self-documenting Make the application self-documenting.
lead-with-examples Put real examples in every command's help.
help-everywhere Help everywhere.
version-and-schema Version and capability are queryable.
point-to-the-fuller-docs End help with where to go next.
streams-are-typed Streams are typed.
output-is-a-budget Print less than you think you should.
machine-output-first-class Machine output is a mode, not a fallback.
say-nothing-on-success Say little on success.
color-is-enhancement Color is an enhancement, never information.
progress-on-stderr Progress goes on stderr, and only for a terminal.
respond-quickly Communicate responsively.
empty-states Design the empty result.
line-oriented Keep plain output line-oriented.
stream-dont-buffer Stream results as you get them.
nothing-interactive-only Every prompt has a flag equivalent.
detect-the-tty Detect the terminal; never assume one.
prompts-are-courtesy When interactive, prompt rather than fail.
handle-interrupts Exit promptly when interrupted.
fail-forgivingly Fail forgivingly.
errors-say-what-next Errors say what to do next.
exit-codes-are-api Exit codes are part of your API.
one-error-then-detail One sentence first, detail underneath.
errors-in-machine-form Errors have a machine form too.
crashes-ask-to-be-reported An unexpected crash asks to be reported.
never-half-write Make state changes atomic.
only-add Add, don't subtract.
deprecate-with-a-date Deprecate with a date and a migration plan.
machine-format-is-strictest The machine format is the strictest promise you make.
single-binary Ship one file that runs anywhere.
easy-to-remove As easy to remove as to install.
secrets-never-in-arguments Secrets never come from arguments.
be-honest-about-the-network Be honest about what leaves the machine.
write-only-where-asked Write only where you were asked to write.
